unit-m3u3.title: Unit 3 · Lesson 3: Multiply by a 1-Digit Number
unit-m3u3.source: enVision Topic 3 textbook scan — Multiply Multi-Digit Whole Numbers (Drive)

summary.text: Lesson 3-3 of the Topic 3 textbook scan: multiplying 2-, 3- and 4-digit numbers by a 1-digit number with partial products and the standard algorithm.

why.text: The standard algorithm she learns here is the same one every later lesson extends — getting the carrying right now saves a lot of trouble later.

objectives.text: Multiply by a 1-digit number with partial products
Multiply by a 1-digit number with the standard algorithm
Regroup correctly: multiply first, then add the carried digit
Estimate to check that a product is reasonable

parentNote.text: Every wrong option here comes from a named mistake, computed in the builder: dropping the carry (34 × 5 → 150), adding the carry before multiplying ((3 + 2) × 5 → 250), and writing each digit's product side by side (37 × 4 → 1,228), which is the textbook's own "what did this student do wrong?" example with fresh numbers. If she picks one of those, the explanation names exactly which slip it was.

nextUp.text: Right to left, and add the carry AFTER you multiply.

cards.def:
**Break the bigger number into place values, multiply each part, then add the parts.**
• 47 × 6 = (6 × 40) + (6 × 7) = 240 + 42 = 282.
• You can add the partial products in any order.
cards.hint: Split it up, multiply each piece, put it back together.

cards.def:
**Multiply each place from the ones up, regrouping as you go.**
• Multiply the ones, write the ones digit, carry the tens.
• Multiply the tens, then ADD the carried tens.
• Keep going left, one place at a time.
cards.hint: Right to left, one place at a time.

cards.def:
**Multiply first, THEN add the number you carried.**
• 238 × 4: 4 × 8 = 32 → write 2, carry 3.
• Next: 4 × 3 = 12, plus the carried 3 = 15.
cards.hint: Multiply, then add the carry — never the other way round.

cards.def:
**Writing each whole product side by side does not work.**
• 37 × 4 is not 1,228 (12 and 28 written next to each other).
• 4 × 7 = 28 means 2 tens and 8 ones — the 2 tens must be carried.
cards.hint: A two-digit step never gets its own two spaces.

cards.def:
**Multiplying a 4-digit number works exactly like a 2-digit one — there are just more places.**
• 1,625 × 3 = 4,875.

**Round the big factor, multiply, and make sure your answer is close.**
• 692 × 7 is about 700 × 7 = 4,900.
cards.hint: If the answer is nowhere near the estimate, look for a slip.

questions.hint: Multiply the ones first and carry the tens.

ex.main: **170.** The 2 tens from 5 × 4 = 20 get added after multiplying the tens.
ex.tip: 150 forgets the carried 2. 250 adds the 2 BEFORE multiplying: (3 + 2) × 5.

questions.q: Which partial products add up to 47 × 6?
questions.hint: Split 47 into 40 and 7, then multiply each by 6.

ex.main: **240 and 42.** 6 × 40 and 6 × 7 are the two partial products, and they add to 282.
ex.tip: 24 is 6 × 4 — it forgets that the 4 in 47 means 4 TENS.

questions.hint: Multiply each place and add the carries.

ex.main: **952.** Two carries happen here — one into the tens and one into the hundreds.
ex.tip: 822 drops both carries. Estimate: 240 × 4 = 960, so 952 is right where it should be.

questions.hint: Same steps as a smaller number — just one more place.

ex.main: **4,875.** A 4-digit number needs one more step, but each step is the same.

questions.q: A horse has a mass of 485 kilograms. An elephant has 8 times as much. What is the elephant's mass?
questions.hint: "8 times as much" means multiply by 8.

ex.main: **3,880 kilograms.** "Times as much" is a multiplication, and 485 × 8 = 3,880.
ex.tip: 493 comes from adding 8 instead of multiplying. 3,240 drops the carries.

questions.hint: The zero in the tens place still gets multiplied — and still receives a carry.

ex.main: **12,030.** The zero tens place becomes 3 because of the carry from the ones.
ex.tip: 12,000 forgets that the carried 3 lands in the tens place.

questions.q: A student wrote 37 × 4 = 1,228. What went wrong?
opts: They added 37 and 4 together before multiplying
They multiplied the tens digit by 5 instead of 4
They wrote 12 and 28 side by side instead of carrying
Nothing went wrong, because 1,228 is correct
steps: The student wrote 12 and 28 next to each other.
But 28 means 2 tens and 8 ones — the 2 must be carried.

ex.main: **They wrote the products side by side instead of carrying.** 37 × 4 is 148.
ex.tip: Estimate: 40 × 4 = 160. An answer over a thousand is clearly impossible.

questions.q: Maya got 4,244 for 692 × 7. How does an estimate show she made a mistake?
opts: An estimate cannot show a mistake — only an exact answer can
600 × 7 = 4,200, so her answer is exactly right
692 × 7 must be less than 692, so 4,244 is far too big
700 × 7 = 4,900, so the answer should be just under 4,900
steps: 692 is only a little less than 700, so the product is a little less than 4,900.
4,244 is 600 away — something slipped. The real answer is 4,844.

ex.main: **700 × 7 = 4,900, so the answer should be just under 4,900.** 4,244 is too far off; the real product is 4,844.
ex.tip: Round to the NEAREST hundred — 692 is much closer to 700 than to 600.

questions.q: To find 238 × 5, you first find 5 × 8 = 40. What do you do with the 40?
opts: Write 0 in the ones place and carry 4 tens
Write 4 in the ones place and carry 0
steps: The 0 goes in the ones place.
The 4 tens are carried to the tens column.

ex.main: **Write 0 in the ones place and carry 4 tens.** Each place holds one digit, so the tens move over.
ex.tip: After carrying, 5 × 3 tens = 15 tens, plus the 4 = 19 tens.

questions.q: Anthony had 27 silver coins and 18 gold coins. Now he has 5 times as many coins in all. How many coins does he have now?
questions.hint: First find how many coins he started with.
steps: Now he has 5 times as many: 45 × 5.

ex.main: **225 coins.** The starting total is 45, and 5 times that is 225.
ex.tip: 153 multiplies only the silver coins and forgets to multiply the gold ones.
